_comment: The libgit2 port campaign's order of modules and its waves, schema 6, as planner run 4 planned them over the whole target, the libgit2.so link unit and the git2 CLI executable, runs 5 to 7 corrected them, and run 8 re-planned them with wavefront 88793d7 and Crustify's granular item kinds, run 9 with wavefront 7c244c2, run 10 re-derived the later stages under Crustify 6f1e04c's rule for the C tests and numbered the foundational modules' waves first, and run 11 re-derived them under Crustify 596b74e's, the C tests holding no export back. modules and the todo waves come from one wavefront schedule of crustify/wavefront/configs/wavefront-config.json in its default, body-deep mode, every module's files seeded, no batch caps; modules are listed by layer. Every entity is scheduled under its C kind (struct, union, enum, function, global, macro, function_pointer, typedef), the typedefs that name a struct, union, enum or function pointer folded into its item's typedefs; the macros that are not API (attribute, linkage and configuration macros, crustify/artifacts/planner/run-11/compose/not_api.json) are not planned. The order of the modules is wavefront's, but that each foundational module's dependencies on other modules are cut before the cycles are, so that the foundational modules come first; every layer is the longest path over the scheduled dependencies that remain.

Waves 0-168 are the wrap campaign's that had started (88 done, 1 wip): kept as they ran, their items those of their batches, each with its batch's kind as objective; run 8 gave their items, and their batches' items, their C kinds and typedefs in place, at the user's request, and changed nothing else of them; run 9 gave their items' release points, which still named the waves as run 7 numbered them, afresh from wavefront 7c244c2's schedule, at the user's request. The 17 wip waves of port modules were closed with the batches that had landed, at the user's request; their items' release points name the waves of this schedule. The todo waves have no batches, and are numbered from 169, after the highest started index, in one topological order of their scheduled dependencies: the seven foundational modules' waves first, as the user asked in run 10, the type-erased ones (deps/reftable/basics.c, failalloc.c, alloc.c, stdalloc.c, win32_leakcheck.c, debugalloc.c) before the string one that calls them (strlist.c), each by the order of the modules; then the other translation waves in the order of the modules, each later-stage wave right after the last wave it depends on.

Each item's objective follows its module's: in the seven foundational modules, which are wrap in every campaign, the items other modules can reach (functions with external linkage or defined in a header, extern globals, and the types, enums, function pointers, typedefs and macros a header defines) are wrap, the others planned for none; in every other module, which the port campaign ports, every function, global, enum, function pointer, typedef and macro is port where the order places it, and a struct or union is port there when no layout user of another module remains (its opaque_after names no other module), wrap otherwise. The later stages follow each item's release points, which every todo item carries as wavefront 7c244c2 records them, their waves renumbered to this schedule's and their modules written {link_unit, module, foundational}: port/layout after a struct's, union's or closed enum's opaque_after (a flags enum has none; compose/enums8.py tells the two apart), port/memory after a struct's or union's memory_unmanaged_after, port/unexport after a ported function's, global's or function pointer's unreferenced_after, each when the point names a module other than the item's own and not ordered before it, and none when a user stays C in a foundational module. The C tests hold no stage back, as wavefront's closure leaves them out (planner run 11, Crustify 596b74e): a port/unexport carries over the in-scope C test cases that still reference its export when it runs, as Rust tests reaching what is still C through its wrappers, and removes them from c/; a test case leaves at the integration of a module whose internals it reaches, or with the first port/unexport that carries it over. An export whose own port passes its point, but which C tests or the harness (deps/clar) still reference once its module is integrated, takes a port/unexport freed by that integration alone, so that no export is kept for good because of a test. The test cases each port/unexport wave carries over are recorded in crustify/artifacts/planner/run-11/compose/carryover.json, as the schedule schema has no field for them. A test case whose body the configured build compiles empty is out of scope. The stages the same integrations free share a wave of the item's module, after its translation waves, which depends on the last translation wave of each freeing module, the run that integrates its C.

An item a started wave's batches hold, or that a batch landed, with that objective is not planned again, and a dependency on it is one on that wave. A translation wave's depends_on is computed from its items' unit edges: scheduled, its module's previous wave and the earlier waves holding their dependencies; cut, the later ones. A module's cut records list every unit edge they cut, each to's kind its C kind. Out of scope: the deprecated git_url_resolve_cb and the GIT_DEPRECATE_HARD-only field users (commit_id, signing_cb, resolve_url, update_tips). A module's external records count its units' references to out-of-tree entities, macros among them, compiler builtins left out, by the library whose installed headers define them. An enum's field_users are empty: wavefront 88793d7 records no enum's constants. Homes follow the conventions: src/<link-unit>/<TU path>.rs, a header module's <stem>_h.rs. Planner run 11's composition is crustify/artifacts/planner/run-11/compose/.
